name: application-radio-groups
title: Radio Groups
description: Mutually exclusive option selectors for forms and settings where exactly one choice must be active at a time.
useWhen: Users must choose exactly one option from a small, fixed set (2–6 options).
The available choices benefit from being visible simultaneously so users can compare them.
Setting a single user preference such as plan tier, notification frequency, or payment method.
avoidWhen: Users may select zero or more options — use checkboxes instead.
There are more than six options — a select dropdown reduces visual clutter.
Options are binary and represent a system state that takes effect immediately — use a toggle switch.
responsiveBehavior: Vertical radio lists stack at all viewport sizes. Horizontal groups wrap when they exceed the container width on narrow screens.
accessibility: Group radio inputs in a <fieldset> with a <legend> that names the question being answered.
Each radio input must have an associated <label> linked by for/id or as a wrapper.
Arrow keys must cycle between options within the group; Tab moves focus in and out of the group.

variants.title: Base
variants.description: Vertical list of labelled radio buttons for selecting a single option in a form or settings panel.
accessibility: Group in <fieldset>/<legend>; each input needs a linked <label>; arrow keys cycle options.

variants.title: Base (Dark)
variants.description: Vertical labelled radio list adapted for dark application surfaces.
accessibility: Dark radio indicator and label text must meet WCAG AA contrast requirements.

variants.title: Base with input
variants.description: Radio list where the last option includes an attached text input for an 'Other' or custom free-text answer.
accessibility: The free-text input must be activated only when its associated radio is selected; it needs a linked label.

variants.title: Base with input (Dark)
variants.description: Radio list with free-text 'Other' input adapted for dark application surfaces.
accessibility: Dark input and radio colors must meet contrast requirements in both active and inactive states.

variants.title: Color variant
variants.description: Radio buttons styled as color swatches for selecting a color or theme option, using circular color samples instead of text labels.
accessibility: Each color swatch must have an accessible label (e.g., aria-label='Blue') since the color itself is not text.
